subject: Secure SDLC evidence — CI access audit and ephemeral secrets proof
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nimbus Security <security@nimbussec.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Secure SDLC evidence — initial CI access & secret rotation artifacts

Hi team,

Thanks again for the SIG intake. Per your questionnaire item 4.2.1 on build system access and short-lived credentials, attaching a high-level dump of the last two CI runs and the consolidated access log (ci-access-log-20271128.csv). This should show GitHub Actions runners that invoked production deploy jobs and the OIDC token exchange entries.

High level notes:
- We use OIDC-issued short-lived tokens for GitHub Actions to assume a short-lived service principal in our cloud (max TTL 5 minutes).
- Secrets used at runtime (DB creds, third-party API keys) are provided by our ephemeral secrets broker; no long-lived secrets are stored in Git.
- Config changes to infra that affect deploy roles are gated by change ticket SUP-4523 and require 2 approvers.

Attachments: ci-access-log-20271128.csv, sample CI artefact list (ci-run-artefact-samples.txt)

Can you confirm whether you need KMS audit slices or the full CloudAudit export? We can provide a signed subset (SHA256) of the KMS entries if required.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0198
From: Nimbus Security <security@nimbussec.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 16:25:37 -0800
Subject: Re: Secure SDLC evidence — initial CI access & secret rotation artifacts

Marissa,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups so our assessor has everything for the SIG: 

1) We need per-job principal mapping for the last 30 days (which GitHub-runner -> cloud-service-account was assumed). The CSV is helpful but we need the mapping column 'assumed_principal' for each run (or the CloudAudit slice that contains the "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity" events).
2) Evidence of ephemeral secret rotation: specifically the TTL enforcement logs from the ephemeral secrets broker (rotations/leases created and revoked), and a copy of the broker config showing max TTL and rotation policy.
3) Change management proof: the SUP-4523 change record link and the approval entries (time, approver email, and justification). Signed or redacted screenshots are acceptable.

If you can provide the KMS export subset for 2027-11-25 to 2027-11-29 and the rotation logs, that should cover the request.

- Nimbus Security (Audits Team)
security@nimbussec.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nimbus Security <security@nimbussec.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 08:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Secure SDLC evidence — initial CI access & secret rotation artifacts

Thanks Nimbus — sending the requested slices.

Summary of artifacts provided:
- Drive link (restricted) with exports: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_example_ci_evidence (contains per-job mapping CSV, KMS export slice (kms-audit-20271125-29.jsonl) and secrets-broker-lease-log-20271125-29.csv).
- Broker config excerpt: ephemeral-broker-config-v2.yaml (max_ttl: 300s, rotate_on_read: true, issuer: vault.prod.redwood).
- Change ticket: SUP-4523 (approval history PDF attached as config-change-approval.pdf). Approvers: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com; timestamps are included in the PDF.

Notes on provenance and controls:
- OIDC flows are logged end-to-end; the per-job mapping file was generated by correlating GitHub runner id + action run id -> OIDC subject -> cloud principal.
- Secrets broker uses per-lease metadata and rotates underlying wrapped keys on lease revoke. We also store signed audit digest (SHA256) per day; you can verify digest against the file in the Drive exports.
- CI jobs that write rollout artifacts sign them with a build key whose private key lives in HSM with limited usage.

Attachments in Drive and local: ci-access-log-20271128.csv, ci-run-artefact-samples.txt, kms-audit-20271125-29.jsonl, secrets-broker-lease-log-20271125-29.csv, config-change-approval.pdf

If you prefer, we can push the signed subset directly to the assessor SFTP or provide a time-limited bucket link.

—Grace
Principal DevOps Engineer
Redwood Inference

Nimbus / Acme team — sending confirmation that full requested slices are in the Drive link above.

Quick checklist we attached/linked:
- Per-job mapping CSV (job_id, runner_id, oidc_subject, assumed_principal) — in Drive.
- KMS audit export slice (2027-11-25 to 2027-11-29) — kms-audit-20271125-29.jsonl.
- Secrets broker lease log and broker config excerpt (ephemeral-broker-config-v2.yaml).
- Change management proof: config-change-approval.pdf (SUP-4523) showing 2-approver workflow.
- Sample CI artefacts with signed metadata: ci-run-artefact-samples.txt.
